summary: The change implements the key dispatch and the calendar, numbering-system and timeZone lists, and leaves collation, currency and unit as not_implemented (an allowed partial). Nothing is keyed on test inputs. ToString and the RangeError path follow the spec. Only one file is touched. Points to verify rather than defects: the calendar names and aliases are hand-written, the timeZone primary identifier is taken from ICU4X's canonical field instead of spec steps 5.b and 5.d, and the Hijri simulated-Mecca and Julian exclusions rest on an unverified claim about CLDR types.
notes_for_next_attempt: Keep this diff as the base. Open items: (1) AvailableCanonicalCollations, AvailableCanonicalCurrencies and AvailableCanonicalUnits still throw not_implemented. The ticket expects ICU4X data for these, so check whether ICU4X can enumerate them before leaving them out. (2) available_calendars hand-writes the CLDR type and alias strings. Prefer ICU4X's own calendar-kind to CLDR-string accessor if it has one. Confirm the claim that HijriSimulatedMecca has no CLDR type; it may map to islamic-rgsa. Julian is correctly absent from CLDR. (3) available_primary_time_zone_identifiers uses record.canonical in place of spec steps 5.b (zone.tab and backzone Link resolution) and 5.d (renamed identifiers). Check that ICU4X's canonical matches the spec's PrimaryIdentifier, especially for the Jan_Mayen/Oslo and renamed-zone cases. (4) The Etc/Unknown filter is a reasonable placeholder exclusion, but explain it in the comment rather than leave it as a lint hit. (5) The ICU error from iter_ids is discarded and replaced with not_implemented. This is acceptable, but keep it in mind.
